lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.unitTitle: Systems of Linear Equations and Inequalities
lessonRef.focus: proving that replacement by a sum preserves the solution set
lessonRef.title: Investigation or close reading: proving that replacement by a sum preserves the solution set

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows the kind of reasoning the investigation asks for.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Talk through what changes and what stays fixed before you answer.

items.prompt: A student replaces the second equation of a system with (second equation) + 4 × (first equation). Which statement is correct?
choices: The new system has exactly the same solution set, because the replacement step is reversible.
The new system may lose solutions that the original had.
The new system is equivalent only when 4 is 1.
The new system may gain solutions that the original did not have.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt:
How many solutions does this system have?
  7x + 5y = -5
  28x + 20y = -15
Is the point (-7, -3) in the solution region of 5x − 3y ≤ -10?
choices: No; substituting gives -26, which is greater than -10.
Only points on the boundary line are in the solution region.
The region cannot be tested without graphing it first.

items.prompt: A student replaces the second equation of a system with (second equation) + 2 × (first equation). Which statement is correct?
choices: The new system is equivalent only when 2 is 1.
The new system may lose solutions that the original had.
The new system has exactly the same solution set, because the replacement step is reversible.
The new system may gain solutions that the original did not have.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Write out the reasoning in full sentences. A correct answer with no justification does not count here.
